Medium-Voltage DC (MVDC) and Meshed MT-MVDC Networks 37 PNNL-38364 5.0 Solid-State Transformers (SSTs) as Grid Building Blocks 5.1 Background and role in a PE-enabled grid Solid-state transformers (SSTs)—also called smart transformers (STs)—combine high-frequency (HF) isolated power conversion with software-defined control to perform voltage transformation and advanced grid functions at the medium-/low-voltage (MV/LV) interface. Compared with magnetic transformers, SSTs provide bidirectional power flow, fast dynamic control, and native interfacing of AC and DC subsystems through their internal DC link(s), positioning them as architectural elements in a power-electronics (PE)–enabled grid rather than merely device-level replacements (Allende et al., 2020; Huber & Kolar, 2019; Saleh et al., 2019a; Saleh et al., 2019b).
